Bug_Details:
Variable assigned to itself The left-hand side and right-hand side of this assignment are the same. It has
no effect. This also handles assignments in which the right-hand side is a call to
Preconditions.checkNotNull(), which returns the variable that was checked for
non-nullity. If you just intended to check that the variable is non-null, please
don’t assign the result to the checked variable; just call
Preconditions.checkNotNull() as a bare statement.
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by assigning a variable to itself in two different methods. In the first method, 'value = value;', the variable 'value' is assigned to itself, which has no effect. In the second method,'str = Objects.requireNonNull(str);', the variable'str' is assigned to the result of a call to Preconditions.checkNotNull(), which returns the variable itself. This also has no effect and is a violation of the bug rule.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test cases call the methods'showBug' and'showBug2' with appropriate arguments. The 'testShowBugWithNull' method specifically triggers the bug by passing null to'showBug2', which results in a NullPointerException due to the self-assignment bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that all tests passed without any failures or exceptions. The test cases did not detect any issues that would confirm the presence of the self-assignment bug, as the expected outputs were returned correctly.
